'''Chien-Pai Han''' (December 17, 1936 - September 1, 2020) was an American 
statistician known for his contributions to statistical inference, multivariate analysis, discriminant analysis, and sample survey methodology.<ref 
name="UTA-obit">{{cite web |title=Colleagues remember Chien-Pai Han as brilliant statistician, kind man |url=https://www.uta.edu/academics/schools-colleges/science/news/2021/08/02/colleagues-remember-chien-pai-han-as-brilliant-statistician-kind-and-caring-friend |publisher=University of Texas at Arlington |date=August 2, 2021 |access-date=January 30, 2026}}</ref> Han held faculty positions at [[Iowa State University]] (1967-1982) and the [[University of Texas at Arlington]] (1982-2017).<ref name="UTA-obit" />

== Early life and education ==
Han was born in Hunan, China on December 17, 1936 and grew up in Taiwan.<ref name="UTA-obit" /> He earned his Ph.D. in Statistics from [[Harvard University]] in  1967,<ref name="Harvard">{{cite web |title=Harvard University PhD Mathematics Dissertations 1960-1969 |url=https://guides.library.harvard.edu/mathematics/dissertations |publisher=Harvard University}}</ref> where he studied under the supervision of [[Arthur P. Dempster]].<ref name="Harvard" /> He completed his Ph.D. in Statistics at [[Harvard University]] in 1967,<ref name="Harvard" /> where his doctoral advisor was [[Arthur P. Dempster]].<ref name="Harvard" /> His dissertation was titled ''Testing the Homogeneity of a Set of Correlated Variances''.<ref name="Harvard" />

== Academic career ==
Han began his academic career at [[Iowa State University]] in 1967 as an associate professor in the Department of Statistics,<ref name="JSTOR-1968">{{cite journal 
|last=Han |first=Chien-Pai |title=Double Sampling with Partial Information on Auxiliary Variables |journal=Journal of the American Statistical Association |volume=63 |issue=324 
|pages=1142–1151 |year=1968 |jstor=2285897}}</ref> where he contributed to research and teaching in mathematical statistics.<ref name="UTA-obit" /> During his tenure at Iowa State, he collaborated extensively with [[T. A. Bancroft]].<ref 
name="BancroftHan1981" /> He remained at Iowa State University for 15 years.<ref name="UTA-obit" />

Han joined the Department of Mathematics at the [[University of Texas at Arlington]] (UTA) in 1982,<ref name="UTA-obit" /> where he became a central figure in developing the statistics program.<ref name="UTA-obit" /> Over the course of his 35-year tenure at UTA, he supervised 20 Ph.D. students and 36 M.S. students,<ref name="UTA-obit" /> and he was known for his mentorship of junior faculty and graduate students.<ref name="UTA-obit" /> Han retired in 2017 and was named Professor Emeritus.<ref name="UTA-obit" /><ref name="UTA-memoriam">{{cite web |title=In Memoriam |url=https://resources.uta.edu/hr/services/retirees-club/in-memoriam.php |publisher=University of Texas at Arlington |access-date=January 30, 2026}}</ref>

== Research contributions ==
Han's research contributions spanned multiple areas of statistical theory and methodology. His early work focused on discriminant analysis, particularly the distribution of discriminant functions when covariance matrices have special structures.<ref name="Han1969-AMS">{{cite journal |last=Han 
|first=Chien-Pai |title=Distribution of Discriminant Function When Covariance Matrices are Proportional |journal=Annals of Mathematical Statistics |volume=40 |issue=3 
|pages=979–985 |year=1969 |doi=10.1214/aoms/1177697601|doi-access=free }}</ref> His work in this area provided theoretical foundations for classification problems in multivariate analysis.

Han made contributions to survey sampling theory, including work on double sampling with partial information on auxiliary variables<ref 
name="JSTOR-1968" /> and the efficiency of ratio estimators under different sampling schemes.<ref name="ChandhokHan1990" /> His research also addressed shrinkage estimation,<ref name="HawkinsHan1989" /> analysis of variance for incomplete models,<ref name="Han1975-AS">{{cite journal 
|last=Han |first=Chien-Pai |title=Power of Analysis of Variance Test Procedures for Incompletely Specified Fixed Models |journal=Annals of Statistics |volume=3 |issue=4 
|pages=797–808 |year=1975 |doi=10.1214/aos/1176343189}}</ref> estimation in random effects models,<ref name="ChiouHan1996" /> and central limit theorems for nonlinear statistics in repeated sampling from finite populations.<ref 
name="TR312" />

Later in his career, Han worked on quality control and process capability indices,<ref 
name="UTA-obit" /> computational statistics,<ref 
name="LiHan2014" /> and applications of statistical methods to practical problems

Han was elected a Fellow of the American Statistical Association in 1998.<ref>https://ww2.amstat.org/fellows/</ref>

== Death ==
Han died on September 1, 2020, following a long illness.<ref name="UTA-obit" 
/><ref name="UTA-memoriam" /> He was 83 years old.<ref 
name="Dignity">{{cite web |title=Chien Pai Han Obituary |url=https://www.dignitymemorial.com/obituaries/houston-tx/chien-han-9346532 |publisher=Dignity Memorial 
|access-date=January 27, 2026}}</ref>
